predecessors.name: Indo-Scythians
predecessors.text: Gujarat, Kathiawar and southern Rajasthan: the 43 growth of the Western Satraps is 1,330 of 1,331 cells cut from the Indo-Scythian shape

successors.name: Gupta Empire
successors.text: Malwa, Gujarat and Saurashtra: Chandragupta II 'conquered Malwa after defeating the Western Kshatrapas' and likely reached 'the Arabian Sea coast in present-day Gujarat'

successors.name: Maitraka dynasty
successors.text: the Kingdom of Valabhi of the infobox's successor list

ledger.x: c. 35: Abhiraka, the first known Kshaharata ruler, begins the Western Satraps in Gujarat and Kathiawar. The infobox gives established 35 and disestablished 415 CE and lists Abhiraka as ruler c. 35. Cliopatria's first shape is 43; the page gives no territory for Abhiraka, so the land is Cliopatria's.

c. 78: Chashtana founds the Kardamaka dynasty at Ujjain and the Saka era begins. Modern scholars widely equate the beginning of the Saka era with his ascension (possibly to Mahakshatrapa) in 78 CE; the Kshaharata line (Bhumaka, Nahapana) was the other major Saka Satrap line. The Kshaharata-to-Kardamaka succession is…

c. 130, drawn from 127: Rudradaman I (r. 130-150) wins back the lands Gautamiputra Satakarni took from Nahapana. The Rudradaman page: he regained the former Nahapana territories except Poona and Nasik, repaired the Sudarshana lake and defeated Satakarni twice; the Junagadh inscription of 150 names Akaravanti (Malwa)…

127: the Satraps are drawn as vassals of the Kushans, the 'early period' of the Western Satraps page (re-read 2026-10-19): 'the position taken by modern scholarship is that the Western Satraps were vassals of the Kushans, at least in the early period until Rudradaman I conquered the Yaudheyas, who are usually thought…
150: the Kushan suzerainty over the Satraps ends.

c. 154: Aparanta, northern Konkan, passes to Vashishtiputra Satakarni. The Rudradaman page says his daughter married Vashishtiputra Satakarni and he gave Aparanta to Satakarni as dowry (Kanheri inscription); the page gives no year, and 154 is Cliopatria's.

c. 184: Yajna Sri Satakarni reconquers the southern Satrap lands. In the late 2nd century Yajna Sri Satakarni (170-199 CE) defeated the Western Satraps and reconquered their southern regions; the Satavahana page says he 'recovered much of the territory lost' to the Satraps and that the Abhiras…
c. 224: Nasik enters the Satrap shape in the year Cliopatria's Satavahana row ends. The Satavahana page has the Abhiras take the north around Nashik; the Abhira dynasty page…

c. 224: the Satraps take back the southern lands lost in 184 as Cliopatria's Satavahana row ends. The Satavahana page gives the end as c. 224 and splits the empire into five kingdoms; nothing on it says the Satraps took any of it, and the Abhira dynasty page says the Abhiras 'gradually seized' Malwa…

c. 260: the Vakatakas take the eastern Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha border lands. Vakataka page: Vindhyashakti (r. 250-270) founded the family and Pravarasena I (270-330) 'carried his arms to the Narmada in the north'; the page does not say whom they displaced and does not mention the Satraps in the 3rd century. 260 is…

c. 270: Sindh, southern Punjab and western Rajasthan appear in the Satrap shape. Page-silent as to date and as to owner: the Rudradaman page lists Sindhu-Sauvira, Maru and Kukura among Rudradaman's lands in 150, and Cliopatria draws the same land as Eastern Kushan up to 269. The Western Satraps page names Rudrasena II…

c. 306: part of Rajasthan passes to the Yaudheyas. Page-silent on the year; the Rudradaman page says Rudradaman subdued the Yaudheyas in Haryana and that they 'later regained independence'. 306 is where Cliopatria's Yaudheya row begins.

c. 347: Samudragupta's Guptas take Rajasthan, half of Sindh and the southern Punjab. The page dates his conquests to no year: reign c. 335-375, direct control 'from the Ravi east to the Brahmaputra, with a southwest line from Karnal to Bhilsa'; the Shaka-Murundas of the Allahabad pillar are read as the Western…
397-409: Chandragupta II fights the last Kshatrapa, Rudrasimha III, for Malwa and Gujarat.
409: the war ends in Gupta victory; Chandragupta II's coins dated 409 resemble Kshatrapa coins, the Garuda replacing the Kshatrapa symbol; his Sanchi inscription of 412-413 records his victories.
409: Chandragupta II ends the Western Satraps.

wars.name: Kshatrapa-Satavahana wars of Nasik Cave 10
wars.outcome: The Nasik Cave 10 inscriptions record Kshatrapa victories over the Satavahanas in 105-106.

wars.name: Gautamiputra Satakarni's war on Nahapana
wars.outcome: Gautamiputra defeated Nahapana and restruck his coins (Jogalthembi hoard, Nashik district); the Kshaharata line ends.

wars.name: Rudradaman I's wars with the Satavahanas
wars.outcome: Rudradaman defeated Satakarni twice but spared him because of their family ties; his daughter married Vashishtiputra Satakarni and Aparanta went to Satakarni as dowry.

wars.name: Rudradaman I's campaign against the Yaudheyas
wars.outcome: Rudradaman 'by force destroyed the Yaudheyas who were loath to submit' (Junagadh inscription); they later regained independence.

wars.name: Yajna Sri Satakarni's reconquest of the Satrap south
wars.outcome: Yajna Sri Satakarni defeated the Western Satraps and reconquered their southern regions.

wars.name: Samudragupta's campaigns in the west
wars.outcome: Samudragupta reduced the forest kings, made the Yaudheyas and Malavas tributaries and may have ousted the Shaka Sridharavarman at Eran; the page dates none of it to a year.

wars.name: Gupta-Saka War (Chandragupta II)
wars.outcome: Chandragupta II defeated the Western Kshatrapas (Rudrasimha III) and annexed Malwa and Gujarat; the Satrap state ends.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the realm is known from inscriptions (Junagadh 150, Nasik caves, Sanchi), coin hoards and Ptolemy's list, not from lines.
